summary.headline: Unimech Q4 FY26 net revenue recovered to ~Rs 82 crore (gross ~Rs 96-97 crore pre-tariff concession); FY26 net revenue ~Rs 240 crore, PAT ~Rs 63 crore.
summary.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as one of the strongest quarters of the year, with sequential recovery in aerospace tooling demand after tariff-related disruption eased from February. Q4 net revenue was ~Rs 82 crore and Q4 PAT ~Rs 26 crore; FY26 net revenue exceeded Rs 240 crore (gross Rs 257 crore) and PAT was ~Rs 63 crore, lower than last year. Order book as of May 2026 is ~Rs 314 crore consolidated including Hobel (~Rs 107 crore), and management guides Q1 FY27 revenue above Q4 FY26. Hobel Bellows acquisition closed in April 2026 and the Saudi JV with Kanoo Group is in set-up; neither contributed to FY26 consolidated numbers.

segments.name: Aero tooling (aero engine and airframe complex tooling)
segments.commentary: Contributed ~90% of revenue in Q4 FY26 and over 90% for FY26; tooling order book ~Rs 100 crore+, executed on a PO-to-PO basis over 4-6 months.

segments.name: Precision components and assemblies
segments.commentary: Contributed ~10% of revenue; ~200 first article inspections (FAIs) done in FY26 with target to double; early production orders received in calendar 2026.

segments.name: Nuclear
segments.commentary: Order wins ~Rs 87 crore to date, mainly EMCCR projects at Tarapur and Madras, expected to execute over 12-18 months; ~10 qualified semi-systems/sub-assemblies.

segments.name: Hobel Bellows (acquired April 2026)
segments.commentary: Metallic bellows, flexible tubing and precision assemblies; ~Rs 107 crore order book; not yet consolidated in Q4 and expected from Q1 FY27; ~12-month visibility; AS9100 certification planned over 6-9 months.

segments.name: Dheya (30% stake)
segments.commentary: DET-500 micro gas turbine reached up to 90% load in tests with 500+ minutes runtime; DET-200 certification underway; initial orders from Tier-1 defence suppliers for two test engines, potentially scaling to ~200 engines. Unimech is exclusive manufacturing partner.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 revenue to surpass Q4 FY26 revenue (~Rs 82 crore net); management reiterated this as a baseline, but did not give a numerical FY27 guidance.
Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to be healthier than FY26's ~31%; management declined to give an exact number and cautioned that the Saudi JV could weigh on full-year margin.
Other income to be very moderate in FY27 as large funds have been deployed toward M&A.
Core business capex not expected to be very significant in FY27; Saudi JV capex to be large, with ~$30 million total joint investment (Unimech 51%), largely spent over first three years.
Working capital days may rise to 150-160 days over time.
Saudi JV expected to break even over a three-year horizon; revenue contribution possible in FY27 or, optimistically, by end of FY27.
Nuclear orders expected to execute particularly in H2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Over 150 CNC machines and other machines at Bangalore facility; no major machine additions in Q4 FY26.
Plant utilisation ~50%; management expects asset productivity to improve over 30-36 months.
Free trade warehousing zone (FTWZ) has all approvals; ICEGATE portal in final stage; customer inventory holding to focus on non-US territories.
Kanoo Unimech JV: Ministry of Investment (Saudi) approval received; facility and machine procurement in progress; pilot leadership onboarding.
Depreciation rising by ~Rs 7 crore per quarter after new facility commissioning.
demand_pricing: Demand improved after US tariff reduction in February; customer inventory rebuilding has resumed, per management.
Unimech absorbs ~5% tariff sharing on parts and tooling consumed in the US market; Q4 revenue net of tariff concessions was ~Rs 82 crore vs ~Rs 96-97 crore before concessions.
Management says no structural loss of aero tooling business despite an analyst's question on a customer insourcing MRO tooling.
Qualified SKU base approaching 6,000; new aerospace customer onboarded and more in pipeline.
Management said energy infrastructure maintenance and localisation in Saudi Arabia are creating opportunities for precision and repair-oriented manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: Is Hobel AS9100 certified and how soon can aerospace cross-sell start?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans AS9100 certification over 6-9 months, followed by NADCAP approvals for bending, welding and detection; aerospace qualification takes 2-3 years or more.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Rs 450 crore acquisition be accounted for, and how will ROCE move?
qa_highlights.answer: Goodwill and intangibles will arise at consolidation and are not amortised; ROCE/ROE post-acquisition is 10-16% but expected to improve as the business scales. Standalone pre-acquisition ROCE was above 50%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nuclear order mix and execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Current nuclear orders are mainly EMCCR projects at Tarapur and Madras, expected to finish in 12-18 months; new tenders are pending and Unimech has more than 10 qualified sub-assemblies.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book stay flat ex-Hobel and is aero tooling weakening?
qa_highlights.answer: Ex-Hobel order book is ~Rs 200 crore+; nuclear grew to ~Rs 87 crore, tooling ~Rs 100 crore+, and precision parts are building up. Management sees no structural loss in tooling.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue baseline for FY27 and Q1 FY27 expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is targeting Q1 FY27 above Q4 FY26 and called Q4 a baseline, but gave no numerical guidance. Hobel and legacy business are expected to contribute growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue miss the Rs 90-100 crore Q4 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross Q4 revenue was ~Rs 96-97 crore within guidance; after tariff concessions net revenue was ~Rs 82 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saudi JV capex and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Total joint investment is ~$30 million (Unimech 51%), mostly capex and infrastructure over three years; JV may pull down full-year margins, but the overall margin profile is expected to be similar to FY26.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 revenue must exceed Q4 FY26 (~Rs 82 crore net); a Q1 analyst challenge on legacy growth was raised.
Working capital days rising from ~120-125 toward 150-160 days, plus ongoing borrowings.
Forex losses on foreign currency borrowings (Rs 9.6 crore in Q4) and currency volatility.
Geopolitical and regional conflict risks, including in the GCC for the Saudi JV.
Nuclear order timing depends on tender releases and milestones, with H2 FY27 weighting.
Hobel AS9100 certification and aerospace NADCAP qualification timeline (6-9 months and 2-3 years).
Low utilisation (~50%) and fixed asset turnover of ~1.4x.
summary.management_tone: Constructively optimistic on FY27 with a balanced caveat that aerospace order execution, nuclear milestones and qualification timelines will shape quarterly phasing. Management avoided numerical guidance, deferring to a Q1 FY27 revenue-above-Q4 target and qualitative margin commentary.

key_quotes: Q4 FY26 has been one of the strongest quarters for the company this financial year, both from a revenue as well as the EBITDA performance standpoint.
Till date, we have secured order wins amounting to approximately Rs. 87 crore in this space, a portion of which is expected to be executed during the current financial year.
I would advise all to assess Q3 and Q4 performance together as a substantial portion of cost absorption occurred during Q3, resulting in comparatively stronger margins in Q4.
We will strive for improving our quarterly revenue base and will target Q1 FY27 revenue to surpass the Q4 FY26 revenues.
So, we are planning an overall $30 million of joint investment in the Saudi JV, that is the Kanoo JV. Our share will be 51% out of it.
